challenges.headline: "Edit the total" left undefined
challenges.premise: The request treats editing a reported total as a simple field change.
challenges.alternative: Model the edit as a traceable adjustment entry — a new, attributed, reversible line that makes the sum add up — rather than a direct override of the derived value.
challenges.consequence: An override silently decouples the report from its own source entries; nobody can later prove why the number is what it is, which is exactly what an audit will ask.
challenges.recommendation: Force this decision with Finance and compliance before designing the data model — it changes the schema, not just a validation rule.

challenges.headline: Closed-period editability assumed
challenges.premise: The request implies totals can be edited whenever a correction is needed, without regard to period status.
challenges.alternative: Gate editing by period lifecycle: open/in-review periods take direct adjustments, closed periods only take a restatement or a next-period adjustment, both logged distinctly.
challenges.consequence: Without this gate, a closed period's figures can be mutated after they've already been filed or exported, silently invalidating everything built on them.
challenges.recommendation: Define the period lifecycle and the restatement path before scoping the edit feature.

challenges.headline: Export treated as a simple share
challenges.premise: "Export the figures for the finance team" is framed as a straightforward hand-off, with no format or reproducibility requirement.
challenges.alternative: Treat export as a versioned snapshot with an agreed format and field set for its actual consumer (accounting system, bank, or a spreadsheet finance reconciles against).
challenges.consequence: If exports aren't retained as point-in-time snapshots, a later correction makes the original export unreproducible — finance can no longer prove what was sent when.
challenges.recommendation: Identify the actual downstream consumer and its format requirements, and decide whether exports must be retained/versioned.

challenges.headline: "Edit the total" is undefined
challenges.premise: The request treats editing a reported total as a simple field update.
challenges.alternative: Model the correction as a separate, attributed adjustment entry that sits alongside the raw actuals so the total still reconciles back to its source data, rather than overwriting the derived value in place.
challenges.consequence: A silent override decouples the report from its own underlying entries — the next reconciliation check, or the next audit, finds a total that no longer ties to anything and no record of why.
challenges.recommendation: Get Finance to confirm explicitly: adjustment entry (traceable, reversible) or override (replace the value). This single choice reshapes the data model, the permissions, and the audit trail.

challenges.headline: No period-close boundary assumed
challenges.premise: The request implies totals can be edited whenever a user wants, with no mention of whether a period is still open.
challenges.alternative: Gate edits by period status: direct edits (or adjustments) while a period is open, and a restatement or next-period adjustment once it's closed and already exported — never a mutation of closed, filed figures.
challenges.consequence: Allowing edits on a closed, already-exported period invalidates every report and export already sent from it, with no defined mechanism to propagate or flag the change.
challenges.recommendation: Define the period lifecycle (open → in-review → closed → reopened?) and the correction path for each state before touching the data model.

challenges.headline: Export treated as a simple download

challenges.consequence: If the export is regenerated on demand instead of retained, a figure sent to finance last month can silently differ from what the system shows today — with no way to prove what was actually sent.
challenges.recommendation: Confirm the consumer system/format and whether past exports must remain reproducible as-sent.
